interactions.title: Candrosa offers a journey into dreams
lines: DM: Okay, so I'm—in the predawn hours, after you've been asleep maybe half the night, Kenzo, you awake suddenly to a gentle tapping on your door. Standing outside is Candrosa, dressed in his silver-trimmed ochre robe, walking towards you with a sense of purpose and resolve that you had not seen before. He carries a staff of white ash with a silver crescent moon design on the top. And as he sees you look, he says, "Kenzo, will you walk with me for a moment? I intend to retreat for a few days to pray and meditate on recent events, but would talk with you before I do."

Kenzo: So I kind of get up and, you know, I presume I'm still, like, a little hungover and a little still. Yeah, yeah, realizing a little bit what's happening now. I'm feeling—so I apologize for—for my behavior earlier, but yes, of course. I look forward to it.

DM: He sort of bows his head, and says, "Thank you." And he leads you out of the inn, into the desert to the east, sort of around the side of the village, to a hidden stairway that climbs up the side of this gigantic rock, basically. The climb is very steep but short, and just as the sun is rising you ascend to the top, catching the first rays of the morning light.

DM: Candrosa says, "Please sit. The view is beautiful up here." You can see the morning light catching off the stones in the desert, leaving everything in reds and golds, and he pauses for a moment and then says, "I need to ask you a question." And he seems sort of concerned and a little puzzled.

DM: "For several weeks, every time I dream, I see a vision of a jade hand reaching out to me, very lifelike, except there's a crack that runs down the palm, a deep gash as if it had been cut in the stone. Every night I reach out and try to grasp it, and every night my hand passes through it as if it were an illusion."

DM: "Until last night. You were in my dreams. You did something to it. You reached out and you healed it. You placed something in the gash, and then your hand closed around it and you vanished. This feels significant. Do you know what this might be?"

Kenzo: One of the reasons I sought you out in Karawa was because I've been very curious about the origins of the amulet of mine, and I've also had dreams. I've also had many dreams. Dreams that I don't quite understand about my past—places that I feel like I've been but also feel confident that had never been. A lot of it, I think, has—may have something to do with this. I pull out the—the piece.
DM: When you pull that out, he looks slightly stunned, and, "That is—that is it. That's—that looks exactly like what I saw you holding in my dream last night."

Kenzo: What's the significance? This is, this is part of why I came to seek you, is to learn more about this stone. I've had it as long as I can remember. And it means something important. I just don't know what.

DM: He's sort of pauses thoughtful for a moment, and he sort of holds up his staff, which you can see this, like, crescent moon design begins to—here, let me see if I can—I paste an image in chat. One second. It looks like—it looks like it's very intricate, elaborate design. It looks like that. Huh, and it seems to be glowing with the sort of silver light, and as he—as he—as he are sort of asking these questions, he says—

DM: The staff seems to grow both larger and more insubstantial, almost as if you're seeing it through a faint mist. He says, "I can send you to the Dreamworld if you wish. You may find answers, but this is not a thing to do lightly, as it has its own perils. It may be the only way to learn more about this item you carry and my visions."
Kenzo: How do I travel there?
DM: He holds up the staff. He says, "Through this."
Kenzo: Are the places that I've seen in my dreams part of this world? The Dreamworld?
DM: A dream world. It's hard to explain. It's like an echo of our world. Everything here is reflected there, but in a different order, in a different geometry.

DM: You can see the past, the future—things that were and might have been, things that might yet come to pass. You can see true things, false things, and things that may yet become true. A world of visions, but also, occasionally, of answers.
Kenzo: Can I arrive there on my own, through my own meditation practice? Something I've been studying.
DM: I have heard rumor of individuals who are able to reach out their minds and touch other planes.

DM: If you could do this, I think you would know. This staff—he holds it up—a relic of our faith, provides a powerful connection between these planes, between our material world and the land of dreams. And through this staff we are able to see visions, manipulate, experience dreams, and connect to that world.
Kenzo: Of course I'd like to travel there. Is there anything that you advise me? How long will I be gone? And what will I find?

DM: I cannot say what you will find. You will be gone only moments. Time does not pass the same way here and there. I would say, remember the staff. Remember your body. Remember what—what being you feels like. Or you may not be able to find your way back.

DM: Before you is a man, robed and hooded, holding a staff in one hand. His other hand, and seemingly part or all of his arm, is made of jade. He looks at you for a long moment and then, in a movement so quick it seems like teleportation, he is standing directly in front of you, his jade hand moving towards you, and then through your forehead. He says, "Kenzo, open your eyes and see." And as he touches you, you are knocked back, momentarily feeling as though your eyes are opening again, despite being already open. DM: Do you want to do anything or just watch, though?
Kenzo: He is—this man and I were just standing together. We're standing there. We saw each other. Now?
DM: His jade hand is touching your forehead. And you are sort of floating above your body. But the man, while he's touching your forehead, is also looking at you, not your body.

DM: He opens his mouth as if trying to speak and then is shattered, split into, like, a million pieces which are held briefly, for a moment, together, as if whoever this is had been split into it, you know, 1000 fragments, and each fragment was just held in place, forming the sort of illusion of a person, which then began to fly in all directions, visions flashing across your mind's eye too fast to understand.

DM: And as you feel yourself being drawn back to your body, as if pulled by a cord, the staff now glowing in your vision, in that moment before you are fully conscious, the voice of the man echoes in your mind: "You are not alone. Seek the stories of the Order of the Awakened Soul."

DM: And you blink. Seemingly but a moment you are gone, and as your eyes open, you realize that you could still sense something of the energy of wherever you were. And you can feel your mind's eye waiting for you to open it again, and the force of the extraplanar power of the place where you were—not still quite sure where you were—joining with your ki, allowing you to reach out and manipulate the world. And Candrosa looks at you.

Kenzo: Just that whole period of time, and while I was gone, and wherever I was internally, I tried to rely on that meditation practice and maintain just the most intensity of sense of presence as possible, in part also to basically, kind of, in a way, and remember, like, map in my mind or in my internal kind of presence, like the imprint of where I was and how I—I, like, like that, that—the nonlinear way in which I got there, but to have, like, a very, very strong presence and sense of connection to that space. So, in a way, just so that I could try to find my way back there easily with it, or to have it kind of really embody—

DM: So as you turn and look at Candrosa, keeping this sort of image in your mind and opening your eyes, it feels like you're opening more than just one set of eyes. And looking at Candrosa, you can see around him a faint glowing aura, churning with concern and confusion, as he looks to you and says slowly, "Did you learn anything? Was that elucidating?" You can see the concern and confusion warring in his aura as he begins to speak to you.
Kenzo: What does the aura mean to me that I see around him?

DM: Sure. I guess you're still kind of learning to—you've never seen anything like this before, but you can recognize emotions and you can recognize you know, the sort of strands of somebody's personality kind of playing out through them, the way that colors move around. I mean, you can tell that, you know, he's—he's, you know, relatively healthy, and—and you can sort of sense a little bit of his, his health and emotional state just kind of coming to you as you watch the aura sort of flow around him.

DM: And what it reminds you of is the sort of physical manifestation of the points of light, of the color, the, the, you know, the points of multicolored flashing moving lights that you saw for a moment.

lines: Kenzo: And the only question—the only question remains for us. I look at—
Kenzo: Do we go north or go south?

Seeker: Find such a thing, so

Delwath: We should bring the spear tips.

Wellby: That—so, you know, it's, it's not my place to say this, but we talked about not wanting to abandon the temple. Possible the temple already has been abandoned. It's possible Shakun's already abandoned it.
DM: Candrosa sort of looks over. "I cannot deny that. But there is more to the temple than just Shakun's presence. There is our history as well, and that I will not leave behind."
Seeker: And also, whatever it is that I saw with Stone Sense, which I don't remember, but some stash of valuables.

DM: And deep inside, just at the edge of the range of your sense.
